content: 1. The study by Guo et al. (2001) in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition examined the role of early markers of puberty (enarche) as predictors of adult obesity. 2. Guo et al. (2002) investigated the predictive value of childhood and adolescent body mass index (BMI) for overweight and obesity in adulthood, published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition. 3. In 1994, Guo et al. explored the relationship between childhood BMI and the likelihood of being overweight at age 35, as reported in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition. 4. Vanhalas et al. (1998) conducted a population-based study to assess the association between obesity from childhood to adulthood and the metabolic syndrome, published in the BMJ. 5. Freedman et al. (2005) analyzed racial differences in the tracking of childhood BMI into adulthood, as detailed in Obesity Research. 6. Joshi et al. (2014) studied the tracking of cardiovascular risk factors from childhood to young adulthood in the Pune Children’s Study, published in the International Journal of Cardiology. 7. Juhola et al. (2011) examined the tracking of serum lipid levels, blood pressure, and BMI from childhood to adulthood in the Cardiovascular Risk in Young Finns Study, published in the Journal of Pediatrics. 8. Peckham et al. (1983) reported on the prevalence of obesity in British children born in 1946 and 1958, as published in the British Medical Journal. 9. Rzehak and Heinrich (2006) conducted a longitudinal analysis of changes in height and weight to study the development of relative weight, overweight, and obesity from childhood to young adulthood, published in the European Journal of Epidemiology. 10. Maffeis et al. (2001) investigated the relationship between waist circumference and cardiovascular risk factors in prepubertal children, as reported in Obesity Research. 11. Hassan et al. (2012) explored the association between anthropometric parameters and cardiometabolic disease risk factors among obese children and adolescents. 12. Hill et al. (2013) examined the relationship between birth weight and metabolic status in obese adolescents, as published in ISRN Obesity. 13. Okasha et al. (2003) analyzed trends in BMI from 1948 to 1968 using data from the Glasgow Alumni Cohort, published in the International Journal of Obesity. 14. Sandhu et al. (2006) studied the impact of childhood BMI on the timing of puberty, adult stature, and obesity in a follow-up study based on adolescent anthropometry, published in the International Journal of Obesity. 15. Charakida et al. (2014) investigated lifelong patterns of BMI and cardiovascular phenotype in individuals aged 60–64 years from the 1946 British birth cohort study, published in The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology. 16. Skilton et al. (2014) found that high birth weight is associated with obesity and increased carotid wall thickness in young adults, as part of the Cardiovascular Risk in Young Finns Study, published in Arteriosclerosis, Thrombosis, and Vascular Biology. 17. Dietz (1998) reviewed the impact of childhood weight on adult morbidity and mortality, as published in the Journal of Nutrition. 18. Must et al. (1992) conducted a follow-up of the Harvard Growth Study (1922–1935) to examine long-term morbidity and mortality in overweight adolescents, published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 19. Gunnell et al. (1998) studied the relationship between childhood obesity and adult cardiovascular mortality in a 57-year follow-up of the Boyd Orr cohort, published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition. 20. Yarnell et al. (2000) compared weight in middle age, weight at 18 years, and weight change in predicting 14-year mortality and coronary events in the Caerphilly Prospective Study, published in the Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health. 21. Joshi et al. (2014) revisited the tracking of cardiovascular risk factors from childhood to young adulthood in the Pune Children’s Study, published in the International Journal of Cardiology. 22. Casey et al. (1992) conducted a 50-year follow-up study on BMI from childhood to middle age, published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition. 23. Julia et al. (2008) tracked underweight, overweight, and obesity from childhood to adolescence in a 5-year follow-up study of urban Indonesian children. 24. Palti et al. (1988) examined the prevalence of obesity and its associated factors in a study published in the Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health. 25. Whitaker et al. (1997) studied the prediction of obesity in young adulthood based on childhood and parental obesity, published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 26. Adair (2007) explored the relationship between size at birth and growth trajectories to young adulthood, published in the American Journal of Human Biology.
